title: The dummy train to Milneburg and the musician who slept through
summary: Dawson describes the little train from Decatur to Milneburg, used for picnics, and a drunk musician who rode it back and forth asleep.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Whew. See, I never saw them. Well, wine and water, you wouldn't know that place out there. Now, they used to have a dummy. They used to run from Decatur and the Lillusion Field. They used to have a little house there at the corner. Yeah. And that was the headquarters. Now that dummy would leave there, and she'd get loaded, and go on out to the Millenburg. See? Right on out to Millenburg. And that's where we had Veshaix and started from going out there to play, went through picnics and things out there we had. Fall asleep on the train, you told me. Oh, yeah. He fell asleep. And we was all out there waiting for him. And he got full of wine, full of liquor, and went to sleep on, had his heart on. And the dummy done went out there, and turned around, went back in town, and come back again. And we, we was looking for him, and the band said, Well, what are you? Let's go out there, see, and find out, and ask the conductor. And you see the fellow, musician down there, there's a fellow back there sitting, sleeping, in the seat there. He said he didn't brought him in town, brought him back again then. And they was basically laid up there when he was finding that thing. No. Yeah. Junk. But child had brought him back up there and washed his face and got him, got him straightened out there. And man, he blew up some stuff. Whew.
